title: Negative News and Investor Trust: The Role of $Firm and #CEO Twitter Use

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow for the primary, follow-up, supplemental, and replication experiments, including embedded SPSS analysis fragments and the manual AMOS model recipe.

requirements.description: Participant response CSVs or compatible final analysis datasets for the primary, follow-up, supplemental, and replication experiments. The supplied analyses require prelimwillinvest, finalwillinvest, condition, medium, source, AFFECTIVE1–AFFECTIVE5, and COGNITIVE1–COGNITIVE5 for documented primary analyses; inputs and fields for other reported analyses remain unspecified.

software.name: IBM SPSS Statistics (authors used versions 23 and 24)
software.description: The authors report using SPSS versions 23 and 24. The bounded PATH probe found neither spss nor stats; installation and compatibility of any local release are unverified. No incompatibility evidence makes the historical versions mandatory.

software.name: IBM SPSS Amos (authors used versions 23 and 24)
software.description: The authors report using AMOS versions 23 and 24 for the manual Table 3/Figure 3 model. No amos command was found by the bounded PATH probe; installation and compatibility of any local release are unverified. No incompatibility evidence makes the historical versions mandatory.

software.name: Spreadsheet application (authors used Microsoft Excel; version unspecified)
software.description: The datasheet says CSV data were processed in Excel but gives no version or preparation recipe. No excel command was found by the bounded PATH probe. LibreOffice 25.2.3.2 is available as a candidate; its suitability cannot be assessed until the required preparation steps are known.

issues.description: This release supplies no participant response or analysis dataset. Author-prepared data availability, route, schema, and coverage across the primary, follow-up, supplemental, and replication experiments remain unverified; no access barrier has been established.

The datasheet says code to convert raw data into the final dataset is included, but the document supplies no Excel/raw-to-final transformation steps or code. CSV processing in a spreadsheet is mentioned; the exact preparation recipe and resulting schema remain unknown.

The PDF supplies SPSS syntax for Table 1 and Table 2 and a manual AMOS recipe for Table 3/Figure 3, but describes rather than supplies similar syntax for other tables. Exact coverage and code for other tables and experiment-specific analyses are not provided; the scope of the selected fragments beyond the primary experiment is unresolved.

Availability and compatibility of the authors’ SPSS/AMOS software and spreadsheet workflow are not verified. The bounded PATH lookup found no spss, stats, amos, or excel command, which does not establish absence elsewhere. LibreOffice is available as a spreadsheet candidate; its compatibility cannot be assessed until the author preparation recipe is known.

evidence.description: Datasheet reports four experiment samples and the CSV/Excel/SPSS/AMOS workflow.
evidence.quote: The data was downloaded as a csv file, processed in Microsoft Excel, and statistically analyzed using SPSS versions 23 and 24 and AMOS versions 23 and 24.

evidence.description: Datasheet promises raw-to-final preparation code at the end of the document.
evidence.quote: The code to convert the raw data into the final dataset and conduct the primary analyses is available at the end of this document.

evidence.quote: Similar code was used to generate the descriptive statistics, ANCOVA results, and simple effects reported in the other tables.

evidence.description: The separate research-materials PDF is labeled as experimental materials for the primary experiment.
Frozen work-item inventory lists two PDFs only: the datasheet/code document and the primary-experiment research materials; no response dataset is listed.

Bounded PATH lookup found no spss, stats, amos, or excel executable; LibreOffice 25.2.3.2 is present but is not verified as an Excel substitute. Lookup is not evidence of absence elsewhere or license status.

Static audit reports no supported code in its parsed coverage; manual PDF review found substantive embedded SPSS syntax and an AMOS recipe, so the audit status is not treated as evidence that the package has no code.
Table 1 descriptive statistics use preliminary and final willingness-to-invest measures by condition.
Table 1 ANCOVA uses medium, source, preliminary willingness to invest, and their specified interaction.
evidence.quote: UNIANOVA finalwillinvest BY medium source WITH prelimwillinvest

actions.description: Obtain the experiment-level inputs and missing raw-to-final preparation contract before attempting the full workflow.
steps: Ask the authors for the complete response CSVs and processing contract for the primary, follow-up, supplemental, and replication experiments. If only an author-prepared final dataset is offered, record it as a potential analysis-only route only after verifying its compatibility and completeness.
Request the omitted Excel preparation steps or code that transforms raw responses into the final analysis dataset, including file/worksheet selection and variable construction.

Reconcile the supplied primary-analysis fields prelimwillinvest, finalwillinvest, condition, medium, source, AFFECTIVE1–5, and COGNITIVE1–5; request the field mappings for any other experiments and analyses.
validation: Confirm the received input route and its file formats, fields, sample coverage, and preparation status against the authors’ specifications.
After inputs are available, run bounded readability/metadata checks and compare the prepared analysis variables with all supplied SPSS and AMOS steps.

actions.description: Complete the analysis map beyond the supplied Table 1/Table 2 syntax and Table 3/Figure 3 manual recipe.
steps: Request exact SPSS syntax or complete executable instructions for the remaining reported tables and experiment-specific analyses; the datasheet says similar code was used but provides only selected analysis fragments.
Confirm the AMOS estimation, missing-data, and output settings intended for the described two-group model if defaults are not sufficient to identify the reported results.
Map each supplied and returned analysis entry point to the paper tables and figures without omitting any reported branch.
validation: Verify that every reported analysis has a documented input, entry point, software step, and output target before execution.

actions.description: Verify compatible statistical and spreadsheet applications after the intended analysis and data-preparation steps are known.
steps: Check whether an available IBM SPSS Statistics release runs the supplied MEANS and UNIANOVA syntax while preserving the documented methods and defaults; the reported historical versions are 23 and 24, but no incompatibility is established.

Check whether an available IBM SPSS Amos release can implement the documented two-group model while preserving its indicators, paths, grouping, and intended defaults; versions 23 and 24 are reported historically, not established as mandatory.

Once the Excel preparation recipe is available, assess Microsoft Excel or the available LibreOffice 25.2.3.2 as the spreadsheet application for that exact recipe; do not assume or reject equivalence before checking the required features.
validation: Record bounded version checks for the exact SPSS/AMOS and spreadsheet applications considered.
Validate syntax/model behavior and the spreadsheet preparation against author instructions before any execution with the study data.

actions.description: After the input, preparation, and software gaps are resolved, execute the documented workflow without changing samples, variables, or analyses.
steps: Apply the author-provided CSV-to-final-dataset preparation steps in Microsoft Excel or a spreadsheet application verified against the recipe.
Run the supplied SPSS MEANS and UNIANOVA fragments and all returned syntax for the remaining tables and experiments in a verified compatible SPSS release.
Build the documented two-group AMOS model with its stated indicators, paths, coding, and source groups, then produce Table 3 and Figure 3 outputs.
validation: Compare all outputs against the paper’s reported tables and figures and record exact runtime versions and any unresolved discrepancies.

review_notes: No analysis_only scope is supported: the package supplies no prepared analysis dataset or verified compatible route to one. A route can be reconsidered if the authors provide a complete, compatible prepared dataset.

The static parser reports no supported code, but the PDF itself contains substantive SPSS syntax and a manual AMOS recipe; has_code is therefore true and the document is the exact entry point/container, not a standalone driver.
The research-materials PDF is primary-experiment experimental stimuli. It is not evidence of participant response data or a complete analysis workflow.

No commercial raw-data source is named, and the work item has no dependency checklist entries. The author-prepared data route and preparation contract remain unverified; this uncertainty is not evidence of a restricted or unavailable route.

The PATH software probe is bounded and does not establish absence from other locations or licensing. LibreOffice is a candidate for the spreadsheet stage, pending comparison with the actual preparation recipe.
